The hero title is a smooth rounded sans with soft neon bloom, not pixel typography; the START button is a modern smooth gradient with a vector play glyph; the notes are smooth rectangles with soft glow. Only the small logo and monospace UI text are genuinely retro. Trade-off: smooth neon reads as 'modern web neon,' while the brief explicitly prioritizes pixel type — the title must be rebuilt as a true pixel wordmark even at the cost of letterform elegance. Clarity & Hierarchy: the CTA is doubled — a 'PRESS START' caption with a play triangle sits directly above a button that also says START, creating two competing prompts; the hollow outlined notes sitting on the hit line read as broken/placeholder rather than an intentional 'hit' state, muddying what the preview means; the D F J K keycaps are uniform gray and not mapped to the four colored lanes, so the control scheme is unlearnable; 'HI-SCORE 9,99,990' uses odd digit grouping; the left column has a large empty band between title and tagline. Visual System & Craft: the title's heavy soft glow plus a dark offset shadow produces a muddy double-image, and a faint stray rounded-rect backdrop sits behind the title like an artifact; the glow bleeds past letterforms and hurts legibility; the hit-line glow streaks slightly beyond the highway frame; the white top-bevel is applied to falling notes but the on-line notes are hollow, an inconsistent component state; the background lacks the signature synthwave perspective grid even though the tagline references 'the grid.' Expressiveness: the layout is a generic left-title/right-panel split; missing signature synthwave moments (sun, perspective grid, scanlines/CRT, chromatic aberration) keep it from feeling authored; the per-letter rainbow title is the most distinctive element but is undermined by the smooth typeface; the blinking cursor block and pixel logo are good seeds to build on.
history.suggestion: One prioritized plan, all achievable in self-contained HTML/CSS/JS: (1) Rebuild the hero title as a true pixel wordmark — render 'PIXEL DANCE' from an embedded 5x7/7x9 bitmap font onto a small canvas (or CSS box-shadow pixel grid) scaled up with image-rendering: pixelated, keeping the per-letter rainbow but quantizing the glow into 2–3 hard-edged steps instead of soft bloom; delete the stray rounded backdrop. This is the single highest-impact fix for brief alignment. (2) Resolve the CTA hierarchy: make START the sole primary control, restyled as a chunky pixel button (hard corners, banded/hard-stop gradient, pixel play glyph, hard offset shadow, distinct hover/press states); demote 'PRESS START' to a small caption or remove it, keeping '— OR PRESS ENTER —' as the secondary line. (3) Fix highway semantics and component consistency: replace the hollow on-line notes with solid 'on-hit' flash states (or animate notes descending and flashing a pixel ring at the line) so the preview reads as live, not broken; tint the D F J K keycaps to match their lane colors and align them under the four lanes; keep the white bevel consistent across all note states; contain the hit-line glow within the frame. (4) Commit the synthwave scene to fill the left dead space and add authored moments: add a low horizon sun and a perspective neon grid floor behind the left column, plus a global scanline overlay (repeating-linear-gradient), subtle vignette, and a slight chromatic-aberration offset on the title. (5) Micro-craft pass: correct the hi-score to 999,990, align top-bar baselines, tighten the left column's vertical rhythm, and give 'INSERT COIN' a slow blink so it reads as a live arcade prompt.
